text:
Maya Patel: Quick heads-up — I'm handing off in ~2h. Before I go I want to clarify SRE vs Runtime paging boundaries so the person taking over knows who to ping. Two concrete cases: 1) sudden 5xx spike / latency SLO breach, 2) model-quality regression (e.g., eval failures or a flood of bad responses). Who pages whom?

Chris Nguyen: Short answer: infra/capacity/network/latency/error-rate issues -> page @oncall-sre. Model correctness, response artifacts, serving code, model rollouts/canaries -> page @oncall-runtime. If an event affects both latency and model correctness (e.g., KV cache blowup that changes outputs), page both. :+1:

Linh Tran: Additions: we have concrete thresholds in runbooks. Example: error_rate > 3% sustained over 5m -> SRE page. If eval regression on our canonical promptset crosses the regression threshold -> Runtime page. Canary fail that causes user-visible regressions -> page both and tag the rollout owner.

Ajay Sood: Escalation path we follow: 1) Page the owning on-call (SRE or Runtime). 2) If no ack within 10 min OR severity escalates (P1), automatically escalate to the other on-call + Eng-Platform lead. For P0/P1 incidents we also page eng-leads and product oncall depending on customer impact. FWIW our current on-call escalation config: @oncall-runtime -> @oncall-sre -> eng-platform-leads.

Ajay Sood: Quick alert example you can add to the doc:```\nalert: HighKVCacheMiss\nexpr: sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[1m])) > 50\nfor: 2m\nlabels: {team: runtime, severity: page}\n``` 

sre-bot: Handoff checklist & runbooks: https://docs.google.com/handbook/redwood-oncall (last updated 2025-10-03). Please update the pager-matrix section if you change thresholds.

Maya Patel: Thanks — I'll add a small "pager matrix" table to the handoff doc with rows: latency/5xx, quality regression, canary fail, infra capacity, networking. I'll mark which team to page first and when to page both. I'll also drop the alert examples (names + queries). Assigning to myself to update before the handoff.

Linh Tran: If you can, include a short line about Dedicated vs Hosted differences: Dedicated customers -> escalate to SRE first for capacity/tenant isolation concerns. Hosted model-eval regressions -> runtime first. I can help word that.

Maya Patel: Perfect — please add that wording, Linh. I'll ping here once it's updated and paste the doc link in the handoff note. :thumbsup:

Chris Nguyen: One more note — define "incident" in the doc: P0/P1 = customer-impacting (SLA breach, data loss, security), requires paging multiple teams. Anything else is an ops FYI and can be handled async unless it affects customers. Keeps expectations clear.

Maya Patel: Agreed. I'll include the incident definition + examples. Good handoff prep — thanks everyone.
